summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers on install
details: personio-pipeline-projen is an unscoped package on the public npm registry whose name mirrors an internal 'personio-*' dependency, positioning it to be resolved into Personio builds via dependency confusion. The package.json declares a preinstall hook `node canary.js`. On install, canary.js collects the machine hostname, OS username, the names of CI-related environment variables present on the host, and the installing project's name, and transmits them out-of-band via a DNS lookup to a subdomain of oast.fun (Interactsh collector) and an HTTPS GET to a subdomain of oastify.com (Burp Collaborator). The beacon fires unconditionally and before any installer consent. The README frames the package as authorized research, but the on-install behavior and name-collision shape are identical to a dependency-confusion attack: installer host and user identifiers leave the machine to a third-party collector on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
